svg.title: Event-driven order processing on AWS
svg.text: Region (3 Availability Zones, all services regional and multi-AZ)
Checkout writes one item; everything after that is events. Black = synchronous request, pink = events, blue = ordered (FIFO) path, grey dashed = failures and operations.
writes each step to the order item, so the
DynamoDB Streams keep changes to one item in order;
a FIFO queue keeps that order per orderId.
Every EventBridge target has a retry policy and a DLQ.
The saga has Retry + Catch on every task.
A reconciliation job flags orders stuck in one
status for longer than its SLO.
1) Checkout calls POST /orders with an Idempotency-Key. 2) One conditional write stores the order; the stream is the outbox. 3) Pipes turns status changes into events on the bus.

4) Rules fan out to queues, never straight to fragile code. 5) The saga orchestrates stock, fraud, warehouse and capture, with compensations. 6) Max concurrency 20 protects the warehouse API. 7) ERP gets changes in order, per order.
